data.turoyo: <...> A šlomayḏi w i ḥubayḏi mqadema l məṭropoliṭ Ḥanna afandi Dolabono w xaṣṣatan hat ste bu waxt di ṣluṯo kobaʕno, d i ḥubayḏi w a šlomayḏi d mabəlġatte li ǧamaʕayḏux! <...>
data.translation: <...> Übermittelte meine Grüße und meine Liebe dem Metropoliten Ḥanna Efendi Dolaponu, und insbesondere möchte ich, daß du beim Gottesdienst meine Grüße und meine liebedeiner Gemeinde übermittelst! <...>

rationale: Adds the unusual mabəlġatte form and a complete explicit l-recipient context to the thin Infectum cell.

data.turoyo: W mbalġənne: ”M uʕdo l yarḥo d l ubetunne gəd mičəkitu bu ḥabis!”
data.translation: And they notified them: ‘From now until a month from now, if you do not pay it, you will be put in prison!’

rationale: Thin existing Infectum cell has two examples after round 1. Add a direct quoted message and plural recipient suffix; this is provisionally Infectum, correcting the reader’s unsupported Preterit/new-box claim.

summary: The existing übermitteln covers greetings, love and insults as message contents. No new numbered sense or light-verb collocation is required.

The Turoyo construction distinguishes speaker/agent, message NP and recipient. At 68/46 the message is fronted and resumed, while the community recipient has l-. This supports analyzing -te as object material, but its number needs confirmation.
The ma-bəlġ- shape at 68/46 differs from entry mbaləġ; the single spelling does not establish a new III stem. Its Infectum context is dependent on kobaʕno d-.
Infectum 42/8 summarizes repeated mediation. The two monks' insults and the cook's substituted greetings establish the meaning from the Turoyo context rather than free German wording.
Jan English is machine translation [MT]. The notification reading rests on the direct threat quoted after the verb and recipient group in the Turoyo.

mbalġənne lacks the secure l-agent material of the inherited Preterit base mbalaġle and resembles plural Infectum with recipient suffix, comparable to other contracted II plural strings. Narrative sequencing and English past tense cannot establish a Preterit box.

The token is therefore placed provisionally in the existing II Infectum box, with the correction explicit in its occurrence decision and example rationale. A new Preterit box is withheld pending morphological confirmation.
The original plus round-1 Infectum cell has two examples; this quoted-content context supplies a third. No new sense is needed for conveying an official warning.
This Jan form does not resolve the different mabəlġatte stem and recipient questions raised in round 1.
Confirm whether mabəlġatte (68/46) belongs to II or III and whether -te is singular/default anaphoric object material despite coordinated love and greetings.
What recipient number is encoded by kombalaġġe in 42/8? The edition's ihnen is compatible with distributive singular reference as well as the two-person discourse.
Confirm mbalġənne segmentation: plural Infectum plus plural recipient, or a contracted Preterit formation? If the latter, supply the agent ending and base correspondence before moving the example.
Does recipient indexing differ between official notification and transmission of greetings, or is this the same message-plus-recipient construction?
Message content is direct speech and the notified people are suffixed recipients. This extends transmission of greetings/insults to official notification without a distinct technical sense.
